title: Apply the width-13 Clifford Gram and its inverse to requested fibres
body:
For the four-qubit width-13 dictionary, the normal operator $K=A^*A$ becomes **256 copies of one scalar convolution on $\mathrm{Sp}(8,2)$** in Pauli matrix coordinates. The scalar kernel at $g$ is $(-64)^{\dim\operatorname{Fix}(g)}/16^{12}$. This gives an executable query for any named output fibres of $Kc$, $K^{-1}c$, or the complete 51- and 52-step schedules of #7809. The source fibres must be supplied with omitted coefficients equal to zero. Dense intermediate iterates are accounted for through an 80-class calculation.

A second query evaluates all 256 Bell coefficients at each chosen symplectic target on one affine-quadratic observation. All targets share one Gauss sum and singleton basis, including for observations outside the Clifford span. The proof gives arithmetic, bit-size and output costs. For a tensor train whose support has been recovered by Ali Romman's #7815, the README gives the absolute-phase conversion for passing its coefficient list to the Gram query.

The tests compare 17,060 transported Bell records and 480 literal tensor Gram entries, including cancellations and complex phases. Every class entry of each polynomial is checked against repeated convolution, and the inverse identity holds on all 80 classes. A separate GAP run regenerated the 81 ordinary class representatives up to conjugacy, class sizes and rational character packets.

This builds on Ali Romman's affine-quadratic contractions, Petalas and Romman's spectral work, alephnan's sector framework and the compiled Bell inverse in #7800 and #7813. The result prices the stated decoder interfaces. The repository's selected conditional exponent remains 0.00363005817.

All 6 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-transported-fibre-gram
```

Prepared by apoursh with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
